bibliographic.title: Evaluation of the Performance of Generative AI Large Language Models ChatGPT, Google Bard, and Microsoft Bing Chat in Supporting Evidence-Based Dentistry: Comparative Mixed Methods Study
bibliographic.authors: Kostis Giannakopoulos; Argyro Kavadella; Anas Aaqel Salim; Vassilis Stamatopoulos; Eleftherios G Kaklamanos
bibliographic.citation_apa: Giannakopoulos, K., Kavadella, A., Salim, A. A., Stamatopoulos, V., & Kaklamanos, E. G. (2023). Evaluation of the performance of generative AI large language models ChatGPT, Google Bard, and Microsoft Bing Chat in supporting evidence-based dentistry: Comparative mixed methods study. Journal of Medical Internet Research, 25, e51580. https://doi.org/10.2196/51580

methodology.study_design: comparative mixed methods study with quantitative scoring and qualitative evaluator assessment
methodology.sample_description: 20 open-type clinical dentistry questions developed by dental faculty; answers from 4 named LLMs (Bard, ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, Bing Chat) graded by 2 experienced faculty members against guidelines and consensus statements
methodology.technology_context: generative LLM chat interfaces (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, Google Bard, Microsoft Bing Chat) queried with clinical dentistry questions for evidence-based practice support

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a rigorous empirical comparison of named LLM chat tools in a regulated health-care domain and explicitly warns against replacing professional judgment and calls for regulatory oversight. However, the provided text centers on accuracy benchmarking rather than conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, audit, logging, tracing, compliance controls, or contestability.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Python triage was borderline_manual with low governance_accountability score (1/3); full-text fit for governance-focused synthesis is uncertain from abstract and front matter alone.

appraisal.notes: Methods are clearly described for comparative LLM answer grading and statistical comparison, but ethics, governance design, and deployment controls are only briefly addressed in conclusions.

cerqual.explanation: The study coherently evaluates LLM answer quality in dentistry, but its direct relevance to conversational governance is limited because governance, auditability, and operational oversight are not empirically examined beyond general warnings and a regulatory recommendation.

coding.theme: Performance and risk of LLM chat tools in regulated clinical practice

synthesis.main_claim: Although ChatGPT-4 statistically outperformed other tested LLMs on dental clinical questions, all models showed inaccuracies, vagueness, outdated content, and missing references, so they may aid but must not replace dentist judgment.
synthesis.contribution: Provides comparative mixed-methods performance evidence for four specific LLM chat tools against guideline-based rubrics in dentistry.
synthesis.limitations: Governance mechanisms are not studied; only brief calls for practitioner awareness and regulatory oversight appear in the provided text.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as borderline or supporting context on risks and human oversight in regulated LLM conversational use, not as central evidence on conversational governance architecture or operational controls.

evidence.claim: Study compares four specific LLM chat tools on clinical dentistry questions.
evidence.excerpt: This study aims to comparatively evaluate the answers provided by 4 LLMs, namely Bard (Google LLC), ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 (OpenAI), and Bing Chat (Microsoft Corp), to clinically relevant questions from the field of dentistry.

evidence.claim: Design is comparative mixed methods with expert grading and statistical tests.
evidence.excerpt: The LLMs were queried with 20 open-type, clinical dentistry–related questions from different disciplines, developed by the respective faculty of the School of Dentistry, European University Cyprus.

evidence.claim: Quantitative analysis used Friedman and Wilcoxon tests.
evidence.excerpt: The scores were statistically compared to identify the best-performing model using the Friedman and Wilcoxon tests.

evidence.claim: All models showed clinically relevant failure modes including missing references.
evidence.excerpt: all models occasionally exhibited inaccuracies, generality, outdated content, and a lack of source references.

evidence.claim: ChatGPT-4 statistically outperformed the other tested models.
evidence.excerpt: Although ChatGPT-4 statistically outperformed ChatGPT-3.5 (P=.008), Bing Chat (P=.049), and Bard (P=.045)

evidence.claim: Imprudent LLM use may cause harmful health-care decisions.
evidence.excerpt: their current limitations can lead to potentially harmful health care decisions if not used judiciously.

evidence.claim: Human professional judgment should not be replaced by LLM tools.
evidence.excerpt: Therefore, these tools should not replace the dentist’s critical thinking and in-depth understanding of the subject matter.

evidence.claim: Authors recommend regulatory oversight for evolving LLM technologies.
evidence.excerpt: Regulatory measures should be established to oversee the use of these evolving technologies.

evidence.claim: Further clinical validation and model improvement are needed before integration.
evidence.excerpt: Further research, clinical validation, and model improvements are necessary for these tools to be fully integrated into dental practice.

evidence.claim: Article is published as an original paper in a peer-reviewed medical informatics journal.
evidence.excerpt: J Med Internet Res 2023 | vol. 25 | e51580

evidence.claim: LLMs are conversational systems using natural language processing.
evidence.excerpt: ChatGPT is a large language model (LLM) that uses natural language processing, an area of AI that aims at enabling computers to understand natural language inputs
